what: {name} is a copper light block switched by redstone pulses.
does: A pulse changes its on/off state, and its oxidation affects its brightness. Waxing stops further oxidation.

what: {name} is an openable copper doorway or hatch.
does: Use it by hand or with redstone. Its appearance changes with oxidation unless it is waxed.

what: {name} is a copper mesh building block.
does: Use it for grilles and decorative structures. Copper oxidation changes its appearance unless it is waxed.

what: {name} is a copper building block.
does: Use it for construction and decoration. Unwaxed copper can oxidize to a different color; honeycomb prevents further oxidation.

what: {name} is a spawn egg for creating its named mob.
does: Use it on a suitable surface in Creative or another mode where you have the egg. Different mobs may need suitable space or water.

what: {name} is a template used at a smithing table.
does: Combine it with compatible equipment and the required material. Upgrade templates improve equipment; armor-trim templates add a decorative pattern.

what: {name} is an archaeology material for decorating pots.
does: Use it in a decorated-pot recipe to put its design on a side of the pot.

what: {name} is a special banner design item.
does: Use it in a loom with a banner and dye to apply the corresponding pattern.

what: {name} is a music disc.
does: Insert it into a jukebox to play its track.

what: {name} is a water vehicle with built-in storage.
does: Use it to travel across water while carrying items in its chest. The storage replaces an extra passenger seat.

what: {name} is a rideable water vehicle.
does: Place it on water to carry players or compatible passengers along rivers and across other water routes.

what: {name} is a bucket carrying its named contents.
does: Use it to place or release the contents in a suitable location. Filled fish and axolotl buckets let you transport the animal alive.

what: {name} is protective equipment for a compatible horse.
does: Equip it on the horse to add armor protection. It is not player armor.

what: {name} is wearable armor for its matching equipment slot.
does: Equip it to reduce suitable incoming damage. Its material and enchantments affect protection and durability.

what: {name} is a mining tool for rock and ore blocks.
does: Use it to mine compatible blocks faster and obtain their drops. Some ores require a stronger material tier; not every pickaxe can harvest everything.

what: {name} is a tool for chopping wood and other axe-suitable blocks.
does: Use it to harvest logs efficiently and strip suitable logs. It can also be used as a melee weapon.

what: {name} is a digging tool for loose ground materials.
does: Use it to dig dirt, sand, gravel, snow, and similar blocks faster, or make paths from suitable ground.

what: {name} is a farming tool.
does: Use it to prepare suitable soil as farmland and to harvest certain plant-based blocks more efficiently.

what: {name} is a melee weapon.
does: Use it to attack targets at close range. Material and enchantments affect its damage and durability.

what: {name} is the full-height form made by combining two matching slabs.
does: Use it for construction where you want a full block with the slab material's appearance.

what: {name} is a half-height building block.
does: Use it for steps, layered floors, and detailed builds. Two matching slabs can form a full-height block. Bottom slabs differ from top slabs for normal mob spawning.

what: {name} is a stair-shaped building block.
does: Use it to change elevation without jumping or to make roofs, corners, and decorative shapes.

what: {name} is a connecting wall block.
does: Use it as a boundary or decorative support. Walls are taller for collision than they look, helping keep many ordinary mobs contained.

what: {name} is an openable gate that connects to fences.
does: Use it to enter an enclosure while keeping a fence-style barrier when closed. It can be controlled by hand or redstone.

what: {name} is a connecting fence block.
does: Use it to enclose animals or mark boundaries. Many mobs cannot jump over an ordinary fence, and leads can be tied to suitable fence posts.

what: {name} is a small hinged hatch.
does: Use it for floor or ceiling openings and decorative details. Redstone can control it; iron trapdoors require redstone rather than hand opening.

what: {name} is a two-block-high openable doorway.
does: Use it to control entry into rooms. Redstone can control it; iron doors require redstone rather than hand opening.

what: {name} is a temporary redstone switch.
does: Press it to send a short redstone signal. Wooden buttons can also be triggered by suitable projectiles, while material affects timing and interaction rules.

what: {name} is a switch activated when suitable entities stand on it.
does: Use it to trigger redstone mechanisms. Wooden and stone plates detect different kinds of entities.

what: {name} is a suspended sign for displaying written text.
does: Hang it from a suitable support and write a message. Dye changes the text color and glow ink can make the writing brighter.

what: {name} is a sign for displaying written text.
does: Place it on a suitable surface and enter a message. Use dye to recolor the text or glow ink to brighten it.

what: {name} is a processed wood building material.
does: Use it for construction and compatible recipes such as crafting tables, sticks, doors, and wooden components.

what: {name} is a tree or giant-fungus building material.
does: Use it for natural-looking construction or turn suitable wood into planks. Unstripped forms can often be stripped with an axe.

what: {name} is foliage used by a tree or large plant.
does: Use it for landscaping and hedges. Harvesting the intact block normally needs shears or Silk Touch; some leaves can drop plant materials when they decay.

what: {name} is a young plant that can grow into its corresponding tree.
does: Plant it on suitable ground with enough space and appropriate conditions. Bone meal can speed up compatible growth.

what: {name} is a rock containing {variant}.
does: Mine it with a suitable pickaxe to obtain its mineral resource. Tool requirements and drops depend on the ore and enchantments.

what: {name} is a metal crafting material.
does: Use it to make compatible tools, equipment, machines, or metal building blocks. Different metals have different recipes.

what: {name} is a small metal crafting piece.
does: Combine compatible nuggets into an ingot or use them in recipes that need smaller metal pieces.

what: {name} is an unprocessed metal resource.
does: Smelt it in a compatible furnace to make its metal ingot, or combine it into a storage block.

what: {name} is compact storage for raw metal.
does: Use it in construction or convert it back into raw metal for smelting.

what: {name} is a compact mineral or metal storage block.
does: Use it for construction or convert compatible storage blocks back into crafting materials. Some mineral blocks also work in beacon bases.

what: {name} is a portable storage container.
does: Store items inside, break the box, and carry it with its contents preserved. You cannot put a shulker box inside another shulker box.

what: {name} is a portable container for combining small stacks of items.
does: Use it to organize inventory space; its capacity is based on the stack sizes of the items inside.

what: {name} is a coloring ingredient.
does: Use it to color compatible wool, glass, banners, leather equipment, and other craftable or dyeable objects.

what: {name} is a soft fabric building block.
does: Use it for decoration, beds, and compatible crafting recipes. Wool also helps block certain sculk vibration paths.

what: {name} is a thin floor covering.
does: Use it for decorating floors and some spawn-proofing setups. A carpet is not the same as a full wool block.

what: {name} is a gravity-affected building material.
does: Place it in contact with suitable water to turn it into solid concrete, or use it as colored falling material.

what: {name} is a solid colored building block.
does: Use it for vivid walls, floors, sculptures, and other decorative builds.

what: {name} is a patterned ceramic building block.
does: Use its directional placement to create repeating floor and wall designs.

what: {name} is a colored hardened-clay building block.
does: Use it for construction and decorative color palettes, or smelt compatible colored terracotta into its glazed form.

what: {name} is a thin colored glass block.
does: Use connected panes for tinted windows and dividers. It is not a full glass block.

what: {name} is a colored transparent building block.
does: Use it for tinted windows, decorative enclosures, or to color a beacon beam passing through it.

what: {name} is a cake with a candle placed on it.
does: Light the candle for decoration or eat cake slices; eating the cake removes its candle arrangement.

what: {name} is a small decorative light source.
does: Place candles on a suitable surface and light them with a fire-starting tool. Compatible candles can share a block space.

what: {name} is a colored bed for sleeping and setting an Overworld respawn point.
does: Use it when the world's sleep conditions are met. Trying to sleep in the Nether or End causes an explosion.

what: {name} is a dead coral decoration.
does: Use it for aquatic-looking builds without needing to preserve living coral's water conditions.

what: {name} is a living coral decoration associated with warm oceans.
does: Use it in underwater builds and keep the required water nearby so it does not turn into dead coral.

what: {name} is a coral decoration attached to a surface.
does: Use it in aquatic builds; whether it needs water to stay alive depends on whether it is living or dead coral.

what: {name} is a shaped masonry building block.
does: Use it for walls, floors, roofs, and detailed construction with a brick or tile pattern.

what: {name} is a decorative stone building material.
does: Use it for contrasting walls, floors, columns, and other architectural details.

what: {name} is a decorative pot.
does: Use it for the pot's compatible plant or item-storage interactions; flower pots and decorated pots have different functions.

what: {name} is a plant displayed inside a flower pot.
does: Use it for small indoor or outdoor plant decorations.

what: {name} is an invisible mapmaking light source.
does: Use it with suitable commands or Creative access to illuminate an area without a visible lamp.

what: {name} is a mob-head decoration.
does: Display it, wear compatible heads, or use it in a matching recipe or mechanism. Wither skeleton skulls are also used in summoning the Wither.

what: {name} is prepared food.
does: Eat it to restore hunger. Cooking meat and potatoes generally makes them more useful as food; exact hunger restoration depends on the food.

what: {name} is a decorative flower.
does: Plant it on suitable ground for decoration or use it in compatible dye, composting, or crafting recipes.

what: {name} is decorative ground or hanging vegetation.
does: Use it for natural landscaping on suitable surfaces. Harvesting and planting requirements depend on the plant.

what: {name} is a small azalea plant.
does: Use it for garden decoration or grow it with bone meal under suitable conditions to form an azalea tree.

what: {name} is a block containing silverfish.
does: Disturbing it can release hostile silverfish, so take care when mining suspicious stone in affected areas.

what: {name} is a developing amethyst crystal.
does: Leave it on budding amethyst so it can continue growing into a cluster. An immature bud is not a full-grown shard harvest.

what: {name} is a light-emitting block produced when a frog eats a small magma cube.
does: Use it for bright decorative lighting. The frog variant determines the froglight color.

what: {name} is a copper-colored light source.
does: Use it for lighting and decorative copper-themed builds.

what: {name} is a thin copper building decoration.
does: Use it for grilles, hanging details, and copper-themed construction; copper oxidation changes compatible unwaxed forms.

what: {name} is a thin iron construction block.
does: Use it for barriers, supports, hanging details, and decorative metalwork.

what: {name} is a copper storage container.
does: Store items in it or use it as part of a suitable copper-golem item-sorting arrangement.

what: {name} is a copper golem statue decoration.
does: Use it for decoration; its copper condition controls compatible oxidation and waxing interactions.

what: {name} is a copper lightning rod.
does: Use it to attract nearby lightning strikes toward a chosen location and obtain a short redstone signal when struck.

what: {name} is a shelf block for displaying and storing items.
does: Use it to organize items visibly on a wall or as part of a storage area.

what: {name} is equipment for riding a happy ghast.
does: Equip a suitable happy ghast to use it for aerial transport; different colors change the harness appearance.

what: {name} is a colored seat decoration.
does: Place it as a seat in compatible builds and use its sitting interaction.

what: {name} is a reach-oriented melee weapon.
does: Use it to attack from farther away than ordinary close-contact weapons; its attack behavior differs from a sword.

what: {name} is protective equipment for a compatible nautilus mount.
does: Equip it on a suitable nautilus rather than in a player armor slot.

what: {name} is advanced protective equipment for a compatible horse.
does: Equip it on a suitable horse rather than on a player.

what: {name} is a chemistry element block used in Education features.
does: Use it in compatible Education chemistry recipes and workstations. The number in its technical name identifies its atomic number.

what: {name} is a colored Education torch.
does: Use it for decorative colored flames in compatible Education worlds.

what: {name} is a reinforced Education glass block.
does: Use it in compatible Education construction where you want a tougher transparent building material.

what: {name} is a hanging cave-vine growth.
does: Grow it under suitable blocks and harvest glow berries from berry-bearing sections.
